Params: Day of Enlightenment, Two Years Later
Day of Enlightenment, two years later, Adelyde's quarters.
Adelyde traces the Helio crest on her white uniform. Two years have passed since Rusalka first gave it to her.

Two years are enough to take the softness from her face and sharpen her into someone capable. The heavy cross cannon that once strained her young back is now nothing more than a familiar weight handled with ease.
Adelyde grows into her role at the Atlantic Eye, and the white uniform makes appearances on a growing number of occasions.
The construction of the Atlantic Eye pushes ahead with relentless momentum, outpacing even the most optimistic projections.

Rusalka's mechanical prosthetics gradually extend across more of her body. Copperfield launches a global exhibition of their bionic technology. Joint public lectures on Erhorn and Kurono's M.I.N.D. technology become increasingly frequent.
Despite this, the four great families maintain their regular exchanges, though people's words grow more guarded, as if everyone is treading carefully around unseen currents.
Two years is a long time, long enough for Adelyde to let Rusalka's invitation to the "new world" fade quietly from her memory.
Her life with Helentine and Arakna continues as it always has: spontaneous boat races, lively sea adventures, effortless conversation among friends... and her weekly visits to her mother.
On New Year's Eve, Adelyde turns down the Atlantic Eye's festivities as she always does, choosing instead to remain at her mother's side.

Unlike the cooler, sharper tones of the manor's other spaces, this room is lit by a warm, honey-colored glow. Potted flowers rest along the windowsill, brought in from the backyard garden. They are the only plants on the estate that have never been touched by a pruning machine.
These two years have also crowded this room with more than just the flowers. Medical monitors of various kinds, IV poles, and a full line of pill cases left by physicians now fill the space.
They sit quietly among the flowerpots and the warm lamp, turning the room, piece by piece, into a hospital ward.
The name of the illness, multiple system atrophy, first reached Adelyde through a doctor's measured tone.

With the coming of winter, the visits have grown more frequent, each one addressing a fresh set of complications. The doctors still share their guidance on day-to-day care, but they have also started to offer a quieter kind of preparation.
"Your mother may not have much time. You should be ready."
Florence lies in the nursing bed by the window, a respirator covering her face, her eyes turned toward the night sky outside.
Only the soft beep of the monitors replies.
Adelyde checks the caretaker's log on the medical terminal, noting her mother's food intake and waking hours, figures that have dwindled with every passing day.
She swallows the bitterness and wraps her hand around her mother's cold fingers.
It's New Year's Eve. The dam's all lit up. They're having the Day of Enlightenment celebration over there.
Arakna tried to drag me along. I said no, and she spent three days flooding my terminal with voice messages... Over forty of them.
The last one was her singing. So off-key it was like the Kelpie had lost its rudder and started spinning.
A soft chuckle slips out of her, cutting off her own words.
You remember Arakna, don't you? The Copperfield-sponsored one. Common-born, but she's got more life in her than anyone at the Atlantic Eye.
She says she's going to be an interstellar explorer one day, captaining her own starship. She makes the same wish every year.
And I believe her. She's already cleared all her interstellar navigation credits ahead of schedule, and she's building a satellite she calls the "Interstellar Drift Bottle".
At midnight, it will go up from one of the Atlantic Eye's auxiliary launching sites.

Arakna is as good at making trouble as she is at making progress. Two months back, she snuck three Huhus from the bionics lab all the way to the top floor of the Atlantic Eye. Said she was training them for "fleet officer duty." Helentine caught her red-handed.
Helentine covered for her, but made her copy the lab safety regs three times. After she was done, Arakna even came to me bragging that she'd found four loopholes in the whole thing.
...I really don't know what to do with her.
Adelyde shakes her head, though her voice carries no hint of blame.
She's really smart, though. In theory class, she leaves everyone in the dust. Even the instructors say she's born for it.
She's a commoner, and Helentine and I are family heirs. But she never let that stand between us. She just fit right in, from day one.
"Hey, Ade, you know when you go all stiff like that? You look like a walking family crest. But when you smile, you actually look like you. So smile more, yeah?"
She pauses, her fingers drifting absently to her chest. Today, she is wearing the white family uniform that Rusalka gave her.
She has not changed since the evening's official function. The crest, where a seahorse bears the sun, is fixed to her left chest, catching the dim light.

And Helentine, the Spelmin heiress, a prodigy in every sense. But she's so gentle, with none of the airs you'd expect from someone of her standing. Every time Arakna lands herself in trouble, Helentine is the one who cleans up the mess.
I'm not a troublemaker like Arakna, but I've got a temper. When I first stepped into family affairs, I clashed with people left and right.

But whenever Helentine is by my side, I find my ground again. And somehow, every disagreement ends with dignity intact. We're from different families, but I've learned so much from her about soft power, about meeting force with patience.
And Miss Rusalka... She teaches me less directly these days, but she sends me out more and more to represent the family on my own.
I know she believes in teaching through action, not words. And I think it's also her way of saying she acknowledges me...
So... yeah, my work, my friends, my teacher. Everything's good. You don't need to worry about me, Mom. When I finish my time at the Atlantic Eye, I'll bring my friends here to meet you.
She leans down and pulls the blanket higher around her mother's shoulders.
Outside the window, a faint radiance rises from the direction of the dam. The celebration fireworks are about to start, and Arakna's satellite array is scheduled for launch.
In the distance, the first firework blossoms above the dam. A silent waterfall of gold spills down across the sea, soft and distant, like an old dream carried across the water.
The past few years have treated Adelyde well. Busy as she has been with family obligations and her studies at the Atlantic Eye, everything has finally begun to settle into place.
She makes sure her mother is comfortable, then collapses into the chair behind her, drained.
Soon, a small rocket will lift off from the Atlantic Eye, carrying Arakna's Interstellar Drift Bottle.
Adelyde waits quietly for it to rise.
Beep beep beep—A series of sharp noises cuts through the quiet. Her terminal starts vibrating restlessly.
Her mother cannot tolerate such noise. Adelyde frowns, silences the device, and pulls it out.
The moment the screen lights up, red encrypted warnings fill the entire display.
<color=#ffffffff><size=21>[GREAT FAMILY COUNCIL EMERGENCY NOTICE: Effective immediately, the Council enters emergency restructuring proceedings.]</size></color>
[GREAT FAMILY COUNCIL EMERGENCY NOTICE: Effective immediately, the Council enters emergency restructuring proceedings.]
<color=#ffffffff><size=21>[The Copperfield family is under investigation for major violations. All assets are frozen pending review.</size></color>
<color=#ffffffff><size=21>Affiliated corporate accounts are suspended, and all partners and financial supporters are ordered to halt business relations at once.]</size></color>

\n[The Copperfield family is under investigation for major violations. All assets are frozen pending review. Affiliated corporate accounts are suspended, and all partners and financial supporters are ordered to halt business relations at once.]
Two more messages arrive, almost at the same time. Both are statements from the Helio family.
\n<color=#ffffffff><size=21>[HELIO FAMILY STATEMENT: \nThe Helio family has always placed the collective good of the Transatlantic Economic Community above all else.</size></color>
\n<color=#ffffffff><size=21>Concerning the serious violations attributed to the Copperfield family, we express profound regret and pledge full cooperation with the Council review.]</size></color>

\n[HELIO FAMILY STATEMENT: The Helio family has always placed the collective good of the Transatlantic Economic Community above all else. Concerning the serious violations attributed to the Copperfield family, we express profound regret and pledge full cooperation with the Council review.]

\n<color=#ffffffff><size=21>All family members and employees are hereby placed under immediate silence protocol. \nTravel outside Helio territories is restricted to official duties only.</size></color>

<color=#ffffffff><size=21>All external interviews and press contacts are suspended. \nAny form of communication or interaction with the investigated parties, their affiliates, or relatives is strictly forbidden.]</size></color>

\n[HELIO FAMILY INTERNAL DIRECTIVE: All family members and employees are hereby placed under immediate silence protocol. Travel outside Helio territories is restricted to official duties only. All external interviews and press contacts are suspended. Any form of communication or interaction with the investigated parties, their affiliates, or relatives is strictly forbidden.]
The words on the terminal blur into something senseless. For a moment, Adelyde cannot process what she is reading.
She struggles to connect this quiet, peaceful New Year's Eve with the cold severity of those announcements.
What happened? Her mind finally begins to move.
The Copperfield family is suspected of major violations. What kind of violations? And for what purpose?

Could the Copperfield family, once the preeminent force in the Transatlantic Economic Community and a name long held in high regard, really have brought about a crisis this grave, as the statements suggest?
Then a chilling possibility rises in her mind.
Another <phonetic=Kurono>tech giant</phonetic> has seen its rivalry with Copperfield intensify since it entered the Transatlantic stage. And at its side... stands Erhorn.
The fractures may have been there for a long time. Today's notice might not be about violations at all. Something far darker could lie beneath.
The official language is pristine, each word polished to legal perfection. On paper, a coup always looks like protocol.
She opens her fellow students' group channel. Messages are pouring in faster than she can follow.
<size=30>"What's happening?? Something's going down at the dam?"</size>
<size=30>"The whole Council locked down mid-ceremony. My dad's line just went dead—"</size>
<size=30>"Keep it down in here. Don't say too much."</size>
She watches, powerless, as the profile pictures in the list begin to fade one by one.
The fellow students from the Copperfield family, the technicians they sponsored. The researchers tied to their joint projects... like a tower going dark, floor by floor, in the middle of the night.
Some of those faces she had seen only yesterday.
—The user you are trying to reach is unavailable.
—The user you are trying to reach is unavailable.
Two dead ends. The same recorded voice, courteous and hollow.
Adelyde turns to the window. The fireworks that had blazed across the sky are already gone, leaving only a dark, empty expanse above the dam.
At the Atlantic Eye, at the ceremony hosted by the Copperfields, Helentine and Arakna were both present.
Now everything has fallen into a silent shadow. A sharp, suffocating unease is swallowing her.
Rusalka's office glows with light, as does every corner of the Helio estate.

Adelyde enters to find her teacher finishing a call. Rusalka keeps her back turned, her gaze fixed on the night outside, her hands joined behind her. Every line of her figure is held in rigid composure.
Adelyde bows her head in a curt greeting, too frantic for formalities. No "good evening," no "sorry to disturb." She cuts straight to the point.
What's with the Copperfield family's major violations? The language is so empty. There was no real investigation, was there?
And those statements the family issued... we barely know anything, but we're already cutting ties?
Sorry. I'm getting ahead of myself.
You'll know when the time comes. The statements Helio released are meant to protect everyone, including you and me.
...I have one question, and I need an answer now. I don't care what it takes.
Helentine and Arakna... I can't get through to either of them. They were at the ceremony.
The Spelmin girl is under her family's protection.
As for <phonetic=Arakna>those</phonetic> sponsored by Copperfield... they're all on the investigation list. The Council's ruling.
She's just a student. The sponsorship is a formality, nothing more. She's never even been inside the Copperfield estate—
The list doesn't see it that way.
Rusalka turns around. Her face holds no trace of triumph, only the deep exhaustion of someone still in the middle of a long, arduous task.
I looked up the family code. Volume Three, Retainer Guarantee Provision. An heir can personally vouch for someone under investigation and request a temporary exemption.
I'll vouch for her. I'll take all liability on myself.
You memorized it? As expected of my student.
The code belongs to the family. And right now, the family's decision is to avoid making waves.
Tonight, the head of the family signed a joint statement on all Helios' behalf. Everything connected to the Copperfields—people, property, every tie—is cut clean.
Filing that guarantee right now would be giving the Erhorns exactly what they need to hold all Helios hostage.
Isn't this strange? Our family leads the industry, and we're staying silent at the moment it matters most.
If that's not enough, then let me frame it differently.
Rusalka steps closer, her voice dropping to a low, deliberate murmur. Every word is carefully weighed.
Every time you speak up for her, it goes on her record: "close ties with a Helio heir."
When they comb through every file—an ordinary student, or one with connections to a family heir—which one do you think they'll make a target?
The harder you push, the more you put a mark on her.
I asked you once what you're fighting for. You still don't have an answer, and you're already ready to walk through fire for someone else?
If I did find that answer, would it be enough to save her?
Rusalka's eyes sharpen, a cold edge settling in them.
She moves to the desk and signs a file. By the time she lifts her head, her tone has smoothed into that familiar, official evenness.
Effective immediately, all of Adelyde Helio's access privileges are revoked. She is not to carry out any official duties without a designated escort. Duration: one month.
Go back to your mother, Adelyde. Don't go anywhere tonight.
Adelyde stares at Rusalka, a great wave of helplessness washing over her. The woman before her is the one most capable of offering aid, and the very same one who has just closed the door.
Rusalka's demeanor all but confirms the worst of Adelyde's fears about those statements. This is likely a targeted political purge.
Helio's public statement distances itself from the Copperfield family, neither participating nor objecting... But at a moment like this, silence speaks volumes.
Helio stands with Erhorn. That is the truth.
Adelyde draws a long breath and walks out.
For three days after her access was revoked, Adelyde has turned every reconnaissance skill Rusalka taught her against her own family, refusing to rest even for a moment.
She has gathered scraps of information: supply logs, family channel notices, servants' murmured exchanges. Piece by piece, they have formed a clear picture:
A passenger vessel will leave from Port A054 at 6 AM tomorrow, bound for the far side of the world.
Those flagged as low-risk in the purge will be exiled on this run.
Port A054 was their old meeting point, the dock where the three of them used to slip away for their boat races.

The instant she has what she needs, Adelyde contacts the night-shift nurse and asks her to come at once. She goes over the body-turning schedule, the doctor's emergency line, every last detail she usually manages herself.
Adelyde grabs the Kelpie's ignition key and heads out without a second's hesitation.
The Kelpie's engine screams at full power, its bow carving through the dark waves.
This boat had once been an arrow, with Arakna skimming it across the surface, spray blasting high and her laughter cutting through the roar.
Tonight, it moves like a piece of driftwood.
The sky begins to pale, and at last the dam's immense shape rises from the horizon.
It's towering like a titan, silent as a tombstone.
Adelyde swings the Kelpie sideways into the slip and jumps onto the dock.
What she sees is a dark, dense crowd. Most keep their heads down, their faces empty and grieving, their feet dragging in one direction with the slow, mournful pace of an endless funeral march.
She moves against the current, reading every face as she passes.
Excuse me, have you seen Arakna Sorano? Blue hair, on the shorter side, smiles a lot...
The person refused to meet her eyes, slipping past her without a word.
Hi, I'm looking for someone called Arak—
The person's gaze falls on the crest at her chest, and those eyes turn cold.
He looks away without a word, sidesteps, and lets the current of the crowd carry him on.
Sorry, I'm trying to find someone called—
The word strikes like a knife, piercing the crest on her chest and cutting into her soul.
The man does not stop. He says it plainly, calmly, and the crowd swallows him up.
Not everyone voices it aloud. Most simply look at her, see the emblem, and turn away. Their bodies lean aside, as if carried by an invisible current around a stubborn stone in the stream.
Then, a body stumbles into her side. It's a man dazed and unaware of his path.
He lifts his head slowly, his red-rimmed eyes fixed on her face.
He answers with a hollow and bitter smile.
Two years ago. At the Day of Enlightenment ceremony. We met once, briefly.
The Helios must be sitting pretty, huh?
Put out that disclaimer the same moment... No blowback, and now you've got the Copperfields' resources all to yourselves...
The faint curve of his mouth suddenly twists into something cruel. His eyes gleam with spite, and his hand darts out, reaching straight for her collar.
The man's grip is feeble, but her body reacts before she can think, her training taking over. In an instant, he is on the ground.
Get off! I don't want a Helio's pity. Ptoo! You're just the Erhorns' cronies!
His eyes are wide with rage, sunken deep in their sockets. His face is pale and hollow, his cheekbones sharp and prominent.
You used the Atlantic Eye as a smokescreen, stole our findings, and threw my wife and me out of our own home.
Did you come here to gloat in that getup?! What more do you people want, you selfish monsters?!
He grows more heated with each word, his gaunt face contorting wildly. Somewhere in the rush of speech, "you" becomes "you people."

She wants to say the Helios are nobody's accomplices, that they only tried to protect themselves, that she was in a rush and forgot to change her uniform, and that she also wants to find out what really happened.
But she already knows how thin that sounds. Too thin to voice, an insult to his pain and her own conscience.
The crowd shifts, pushing from behind. She grabs him by the arm and yanks him up just in time.
The wild fury fades from his face, replaced by that mournful stillness again. He drops his head, shoulders folding inward under the weight of his own sorrow.
Adelyde has never found it so hard to form a single word.
I... I want to help. My friend is one of you... I'm trying to find her too. Her name is Arakna Sorano. Here's her photo...
Oh? A friend? So even the Helios' friends are caught up in this now?
The young man lets out a mocking laugh.
I don't know her. But if she's leaving today, this is where everyone would be.
There's more than one ship, you know. Transports at four, at five. Your friend could've already been on one of them.
She feels the ache in her chest, as though something is tearing open inside her, but she pushes through it. She presses forward against the tide, eyes fixed on the faces that stream past.
In the dark and endless mass, she is only a tiny point of light, swept along by a greater current.
At last, she reaches the end of the line.
A sliver of dawn is already creeping along the horizon, spilling a thin, reluctant light into the world. The glow reaches only as far as the dark clouds gathering far ahead.
Whoa, Addie, still charging in like a bull. Here, how about a hug to prove I'm still kicking?

You're supposed to grab me and cry your eyes out, saying, "Arakna, you made it! I'm so glad. We're going to be best friends forever, and promise me you'll never pull a stunt like that again, okay?" And I'll say, "Okay—"
Adelyde quietly sidestepped the blue-haired girl, who was still mid-monologue, and walked on ahead.
A few scattered flames licked at the last of the fuel, blackening the ground beneath. Twisted metal frames lay slumped nearby, a clear testament to failure.
So this is your "Interstellar Drift Bottle" test launch?
Yup. As you can see, the vector nozzle was off by a fraction of a second. Attitude control couldn't fix it, so it just started spinning and yeeted itself out. Probably landed thirty meters away.
The blue-haired girl wore an awkward smile.
Don't do something that reckless ever again.
Hehe, I don't mind you showing me a little more care.
She said it with a grin, but her eyes held no trace of humor.
There's real treasure in this drift bottle, you know.
Like the sound of us three yelling on the boat, Huhu's cry, the Atlantic Ocean's waves...
Watching her count each item off on her fingers with such earnest seriousness, Adelyde, ever the pragmatist, could not help but speak up.
Of course! They're the most, most precious things I have in the world.
The blue-haired girl wore an expression of utter seriousness. Adelyde, on the other hand, had no idea what she was talking about.
Oh! Almost forgot, there's one more thing hidden in there. A really important message—
"Hello, I'm Arakna from Earth. I'll come visit you all in a starship someday."
She tilted her head back, cupped her hands around her mouth, and shouted it up at the sky with all her strength. Adelyde followed her gaze upward.
There they were, the stars, silent and peaceful. Against the ruined satellite launch site below, the sky above felt like a different world entirely.
Erhorn, Copperfield, Helio, Spelmin, Kowloong, Akdilek... people from everywhere, even when they're far apart, all working together toward the same dream.
Everyone giving it their all, no matter where they come from or who they stand with... isn't that the most precious thing about the Golden Age?
That's why I'm going to the stars.
And I'm taking everyone with me.
The usually spirited girl then fell quiet, her gaze fixed on the sky with a look of pure devotion.
Okay, but you have to keep yourself safe. I'll be at home with my mom on Day of Enlightenment, so... I probably won't be there.
Aww, no way? So you're going to miss my wish-making machine's launch in person?
Faced with such earnest sincerity, Adelyde did not know how to respond. But Arakna was already moving the conversation along.
It's cool though! Once they launch, you'll be able to see them from anywhere. Alright, I gotta go back into my hermit mode. Got to make this year's Day of Enlightenment deadline.
Oh yeah, I just finished tweaking the adaptive hydrodynamics on the Kelpie. Don't go full throttle the first time out. You always rush, you know?
Here, this is a picture of the stars from my last successful launch. Give it to your mom, so she can still see the stars even at home.

That day, Arakna rambled on for what felt like hours, covering everything from Adelyde's childhood embarrassments to how they would keep in touch after settling on Mars. Then she was gone, back into her lab.
She realizes, in retrospect, that was the last time she saw Arakna before today.
The reality is, Arakna is not here now.
The reality is, she has poured years into interstellar flight technology, but the satellite array that was supposed to validate it never launched.
Then the Purge arrived, sudden and merciless.
Humanity's dream of standing united beneath the stars shatters in an instant, leaving a pall over the broken heavens.
Day has broken fully now. Sunlight spills across the Atlantic Eye, across the empty docks, across the spot where wish tags had hung just last year.
They should still be there on the Wishing Platform: one for a successful review, one for a starship, one giving thanks to the instruments they cared for.
Overnight, the hands that wrote them have scattered to opposite ends of the ocean.
So this is how easily it all falls apart.
For the first time, she feels as though she has won nothing. All the effort she has poured into pushing herself to the limit, and the only result is arriving on time at an empty dock.
Is what she has believed in all this time actually right?
This game was never meant to have a winner.
The sea wind carries the damp, cold breath of the tide.
The great structure of the Atlantic Eye gleams under the rising sun, as magnificent as ever, as if nothing at all has changed.
